Let’s dive into Chapter 6: Building a Mindset for Multiplication.
So, you’ve got the foundational principles set. Now comes the exciting part—shaping the way you think, so you’re really ready for growth and multiplication.
See, this isn’t just about wishing for more. It’s about preparing your heart and mind to handle greater responsibility, to be ready when bigger opportunities show up.
The Bible often talks about seeds and harvests—about how what you plant, with care and faithfulness, can multiply into something way bigger than you started with.
Here’s where it all begins: expectation.
Instead of thinking that your current situation is set in stone, try looking around for ways to grow what you already have. Maybe it’s picking up a new skill, brainstorming creative ideas, or investing in relationships that open new doors. The trick is to see every resource—your time, your money, your influence—as a seed packed with potential.
There are some habits that really help build this kind of mindset:
First, embrace learning and adaptability. Stay open to new ideas, feedback, and changes, even when it’s uncomfortable. Growth usually means letting go of the old and being willing to try something different.
Second, set stretch goals. Don’t just aim for what’s comfortable or safe. Challenge yourself with goals that actually require some faith and effort.
Next, celebrate small wins. Every bit of progress matters. When you notice and give thanks for those little steps, you build up momentum and confidence for the bigger ones.
And always be on the lookout for ways to add value—whether you’re at work, in your community, or with your family. When you focus on serving and improving the lives of others, multiplication tends to follow.
Let’s put this into a real-world picture.
Imagine someone starting a small business with just a handful of resources. By serving their customers well, reinvesting profits, and learning from mistakes, that business starts to grow—slowly at first, but steadily. What began as a side project can eventually become a source of jobs and a blessing to many.
Of course, having a multiplication mindset also means being willing to take some calculated risks. Growth rarely happens if you always stay in your comfort zone. Think about the parable of the talents: the people who step out and put what they have to work—rather than sitting on it out of fear—are the ones who see real increase.
And here’s something to really pay attention to—a multiplication mindset isn’t about striving or feeling anxious. It’s rooted in trust: believing that God actually delights in multiplying what you offer in faith.
Your job is to plant, water, and tend those seeds. The growth? That comes from a source bigger than you.
There’s a freedom in that—you’re not carrying the pressure to make everything happen. But there’s also a responsibility to do your part, to steward every opportunity well.
So, by working on this mindset, you can move from just surviving… to living in abundance. From simply collecting… to multiplying.
The journey’s ongoing. There’ll be challenges, and there’ll be breakthroughs. But you can walk it with the confidence that there’s always more available than what you see right now.
